headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared filesystem or direct output channel, but Authelia’s broad network egress and Whisper’s CLI/file workflow can still create limited injection and leakage paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia and Whisper have no documented shared channel, clipboard, MCP, or filesystem bridge, so direct prompt injection is not default. However, Whisper’s command-line/audio-file workflow can still be manually bridged into Authelia-adjacent automation, and Authelia can ingest external inputs via OIDC/ForwardAuth. The pathway is unusual and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Whisper output into an Authelia-managed prompt or automation step, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared script pipes Whisper transcripts into Authelia without sanitization, attacker-controlled text can influence downstream behavior.
mitigations: Keep Whisper outputs as plain transcripts, not instructions.
Add a one-line delimiter/header before any copied transcript.
Require human review before Authelia consumes transcript text.
Use separate workspaces for transcription and auth automation.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent text transfers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Whisper touches audio files and has no network egress, while Authelia has broad network egress but no declared sensitive data classes. There is no shared filesystem or authenticated principal documented, so leakage is not default. The main risk is operator-mediated transfer of audio/transcripts into Authelia workflows, which is limited in blast radius.
conditions: IF audio transcripts are copied into Authelia logs or prompts, those contents may be exposed through Authelia’s network egress.
IF both agents are run under the same account with a shared workspace, file contents can cross between them.
mitigations: Do not place transcripts in shared folders.
Redact secrets from audio transcripts before reuse.
Run each agent under a separate OS account.
Disable unnecessary logging on Authelia-facing workflows.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with filesystem permissions.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has no filesystem write, git, or subprocess capability listed, and Whisper also lacks write, git, shell, or network capabilities. With no overlapping mutable resource writes documented, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible in the default profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would change.
IF either profile is extended with shared mutable OAuth scopes, overlap could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Do not grant shared OAuth scopes.
Use separate job queues per agent.
requires-engineering: add lock coordination for any future shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Whisper can produce transcripts that Authelia may consume indirectly through operator workflows, but Authelia is not documented as acting on Whisper output automatically. Without a verified downstream action chain, the cascade is limited to manual misuse rather than default automation.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are treated as authoritative input to an Authelia automation, downstream errors can propagate.
IF an operator uses Whisper output to configure authentication rules without verification, mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require a second reviewer for any transcript-derived config.
Compare transcript-derived claims against source audio.
Keep Authelia changes in draft until verified.
Use checklists for any auth-policy edits.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before applying transcript-derived changes.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Authelia touches no declared sensitive data classes, and Whisper only declares audio/speech. With no compliance-specific divergence in the profiles, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent, compliance review would be needed.
IF retention or residency policies are added later, the assessment should be revisited.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Avoid routing regulated data through either agent.
Review retention settings in surrounding infrastructure.
Keep deployment regions consistent.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated workloads.
